platforms.name: Microsoft Copilot Studio
details: **Windows 365 for Agents MCP server — GA (June 2026, backfilled after our 2026-07-08 capture)** — an MCP server giving an agent full operational control of a Windows 365 Cloud PC: mouse (click/double/right/five-button), pixel-precise drag-and-drop, scrolling, keyboard typing and multi-key shortcuts, full-screen or cropped PNG screenshots, OCR with per-region confidence and bounding boxes, browser automation via Microsoft Edge, and semantic UI inspection via Windows UI Automation. Sessions allocate a Cloud PC resource and return a `sessionId`; an MCP request is required at least every 30 minutes to avoid idle eviction. File-input setting is restricted to Documents, Downloads, Desktop and `%TEMP%`. Source: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-copilot-studio/mcp-windows-365-agents-work-iq

**Foundry IQ knowledge connection (preview)** — agents in the new agent experience can be grounded in a knowledge base already built and tuned in Azure AI Foundry. Source: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-copilot-studio/agents-experience/foundry-iq-connect

**Agent-to-agent delegation in the new agent experience (preview)** — connect other agents so a single front-door agent routes requests to specialist agents. Source: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-copilot-studio/agents-experience/authoring-add-other-agents

**Voice agents with Teams Phone Agent (preview)** — handoff between Teams Phone Agent and a custom voice agent for specialised call workflows (billing, prescription refills, order status). Source: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-copilot-studio/voice-teams-phone-agent
**Claude Sonnet 5 and GPT-5.5 Chat selectable as an agent's primary AI model (GA)**. Source: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-copilot-studio/authoring-select-agent-model
*(Held below bar: condition groups in Message/Question/prompt nodes — an authoring convenience.)*

platforms.name: Microsoft 365 Copilot
details: **Insights Agent (preview)** — a new first-party agent listed under "Create and manage agents" in the extensibility documentation; not present in the 2026-07-08 capture (page `updated_at` advanced 2026-06-17 → 2026-07-29). Source: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-365/copilot/extensibility/insights-agent-overview

platforms.name: Amazon Bedrock AgentCore
details: **Runtime: Instances compute type with capacity providers (August 2026)** — agents run on AWS-managed EC2 infrastructure in the customer's own AWS account. A capacity provider specifies OS, allowed instance types, networking and storage; AgentCore handles provisioning, scaling and teardown. Persistent sessions up to **14 days**, GPU-accelerated instance types, and **multiple agents collaborating on a shared instance**. Linux `x86_64`/`arm64` at launch. New data-plane operation observed: `DeleteCapacityProviderSession`. Source: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock-agentcore/latest/devguide/runtime-instances-how-it-works.html

**AWS Agent Registry launches on the `agent-registry` namespace (August 6, 2026)** — out of preview and off `bedrock-agentcore`. A private, governed catalog of agents, tools, skills, MCP servers and custom resources, exposed through the console, control-plane and data-plane APIs, and the registry's own **MCP endpoint**. Adds `ListDiscoverableRegistryRecords`, `BatchGetDiscoverableRegistryRecord`, record tagging, a required `recordType`, and a unified Record directory console page. Definitions are validated against the MCP and A2A schemas. Each registry carries an authorization config and an approval config controlling whether records need manual review before becoming discoverable. Nine AWS Regions. Source: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock-agentcore/latest/devguide/registry-key-capabilities.html

**Gateway: configurable rate limits (August 2026)** — customer-defined limits replacing service-managed-only defaults. Limits declare `dimensionKeys` and `entries` over JWT claims (`$.context.jwt.sub`), IAM principals (`iam.sourceIdentity`), target names, tool names and qualified model IDs. Three enforcement metrics: requests (RPS/RPM), tokens (TPM, with pre-check estimation and post-response reconciliation), and new connections/sec. Wildcard catch-alls, most-specific-match-wins, AND semantics across limits, effective rate `min(service, customer)`, and `rate=0` as an explicit block. Config propagates in ~30 seconds and the system **fails open** on transient enforcement errors. Six new operations: `CreateRateLimit`, `GetRateLimit`, `UpdateRateLimit`, `DeleteRateLimit`, `ListRateLimits`, `BatchPutRateLimitEntries`. Source: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock-agentcore/latest/devguide/gateway-rate-limits.html

**Identity: Private Key JWT client authentication (July 2026)** — agents authenticate to a downstream IdP's token endpoint with a signed JWT client assertion instead of a shared OAuth client secret. The public key is registered with the IdP; the private key stays in AWS KMS and every signing operation is recorded in CloudTrail. Works across M2M, on-behalf-of and user-delegated flows; RS256, PS256, ES256. Source: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock-agentcore/latest/devguide/private-key-jwt.html

**Evaluations: expanded agent framework support (July 2026)** — now evaluates agents built with **OpenAI Agents, LlamaIndex, Google ADK and the Claude Agent SDK** in addition to Strands and LangGraph, each via its OpenTelemetry or OpenInference instrumentation. Adds generic framework support for any agent emitting OTel GenAI or OpenInference semantic conventions. Source: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock-agentcore/latest/devguide/supported-frameworks.html

**Runtime: unified span destination (July 2026)** — agents deliver spans to their own CloudWatch log group (`/aws/bedrock-agentcore/runtimes/<agent_id>-<endpoint_name>`, `spans` stream) instead of the shared `aws/spans` group. Controlled by `UNIFIED_TRACES_DESTINATION_ENABLED`; **default for agents created on or after July 20, 2026**. Source: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock-agentcore/latest/devguide/observability-configure.html

platforms.name: ChatGPT Enterprise (OpenAI)
details: **GPT-5.6 model family — GA July 9, 2026** — `gpt-5.6-sol` (frontier reasoning / long-horizon agentic), `gpt-5.6-terra` (balanced), `gpt-5.6-luna` (fast/low-cost); bare `gpt-5.6` routes to Sol. 1.05M-token context, 128K max output, text+image input, streaming, structured outputs, function calling, file search, web search, prompt caching; reasoning effort ladder `none`/`low`/`medium`/`high`/`xhigh`/`max`. Self-serve on the Responses API and client SDKs, no waitlist. This closes the forward-watch opened 2026-07-08. Source: https://openai.com/index/gpt-5-6/

**Codex Agent Plugins with multi-catalog search (CLI 0.146.0 July 29 / 0.147.0 August 7)** — a plugin is an installable workflow bundle packaging **skills, optional app integrations and MCP server configuration**. Installable from the official Plugin Directory (shared with ChatGPT), a repo marketplace at `$REPO_ROOT/.agents/plugins/marketplace.json`, or a personal marketplace at `~/.agents/plugins/marketplace.json`. Source: https://developers.openai.com/codex/plugins

**Sign in with ChatGPT — live beta August 2, 2026** — OpenAI's first cross-platform identity system, with Airtable, GitLab, HubSpot, Notion, Supabase and Vercel as named launch partners, plus OpenAI Academy and Codex Sites. Relying parties receive name, email address and profile picture. Available globally to authenticated ChatGPT users **including Enterprise organisation members**, subject to org admin settings. Source: https://help.openai.com/en/articles/20001410-sign-in-with-chatgpt

**Content provenance checks API (SDK v2.52.0 / v7.3.0, July 31, 2026)** — programmatic verification of C2PA Content Credentials and Google SynthID watermarks on images and (since July) audio generated via ChatGPT, Codex and the OpenAI API. Source: https://openai.com/index/advancing-content-provenance/

**Codex MCP protocol 2026-07-28 support with paginated discovery, executor-provided skills discovery, and remote WebSocket code-mode connections**; plus Cursor skill migration and Claude conversation synchronisation. Source: https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/changelog

**Codex automatic approval reviews** — `--approve-for-me` (0.147.0) with "safer automatic-review defaults for cyber-capable models" shipped as a patch two days earlier (0.146.1). Source: https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/changelog

platforms.name: Claude Enterprise (Anthropic)
details: **Inference hooks — beta for Claude Enterprise (August 5, 2026)** — point Claude at your organisation's AI security server; each governed prompt across **claude.ai, Cowork and Claude Code** is held for that server's allow/deny verdict before inference proceeds. Requests are signed, failure handling is configurable, and every denial is recorded in the compliance Activity Feed. Source: https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/inference-hooks

**Claude Opus 5 (`claude-opus-5`) — July 24, 2026** — 1M-token context (both default and maximum), 128k max output, thinking on by default, $5/$25 per MTok. Available on the Claude API, **Claude in Amazon Bedrock, Claude on Google Cloud (Vertex), and Claude in Microsoft Foundry**. Effort is the primary steering control across `low`/`medium`/`high`/`xhigh`/`max`. Source: https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/about-claude/models/whats-new-opus-5

**Claude Enterprise user management via the Admin API — beta (July 14, 2026)** — list members and look them up by email, change roles, remove members, send and withdraw invites, manage groups and group membership, and read custom roles. Groups and custom roles require the `ce-user-management-2026-07-13` beta header; an Admin API key with `read:org_audit` can call every user-management `GET`. Source: https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/manage-claude/user-management

**Mid-conversation tool changes — beta (July 24, 2026)** — add or remove tools between turns of a conversation while preserving the prompt cache, on Fable 5, Mythos 5, Opus 4.8 and Opus 5. Header `mid-conversation-tool-changes-2026-07-01`. Source: https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/release-notes/api

**Managed Agents lifecycle webhooks extended to environments and memory stores (July 22, 2026)** — four `environment.*` and three `memory_store.*` event types, on top of the agent/deployment/deployment-run events added June 30. Sessions can also now be seeded with `initial_events` (up to 50 `user.message` / `user.define_outcome` events, starting the agent loop in the same call), and session **thread** streams support event deltas that preview a subagent's text as it is generated. Source: https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/webhooks

**Dreams — research preview (backlog recovery; live since ~April 2026)** — `POST /v1/dreams` runs an asynchronous job over one memory store plus 1–100 past session transcripts and emits a **new derived memory store** with duplicates merged, stale entries replaced and new insights surfaced. Resources carry `drm_01…` IDs and `pending`/`running`/`completed`/`failed`/`canceled` states, with list, cancel and archive endpoints; gated by the `dreaming-2026-04-21` beta header. Source: https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/managed-agents/dreams

platforms.name: Google Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform (formerly Vertex AI)
details: **AlphaEvolve optimization service — GA (August 2026)** — a code optimization and discovery agent built on Gemini. From a baseline seed algorithm it generates mutated candidate programs server-side, while the **customer's evaluator runs client-side on their own infrastructure** and submits scores back, iterating until convergence on optimized, human-readable code. Source: https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini/enterprise/docs/alphaevolve/developer-guide/overview

**Memory Bank — Memory Profiles GA (July 2026)** — structured profiles are data structures with fixed, user-defined schemas that LLMs populate and update, generated through the same `GenerateMemories` and `IngestEvents` paths as natural-language memories, giving agents low-latency in-session access without search. Memory Bank and Sessions multi-regional and global endpoints also reached GA. Source: https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini-enterprise-agent-platform/scale/memory-bank/profiles

**Feedback service — Preview, and `user.id` in agent logs (July 2026)** — the Feedback service collects, analyses and manages end-user qualitative feedback (thumbs up/down sentiment and feedback labels) from agent–user interactions; separately, prompt-input and response-output agent logs now include a `user.id` field when that logging is enabled. Source: https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini-enterprise-agent-platform/release-notes
*(Not reported: the July SSRF fix in the Agent Studio `/api-proxy` endpoint is a security fix, not a new capability. Gemini 3.5 Flash removal and the Grok 4.1 shutdown are deprecations.)*

platforms.name: Cursor
details: **Google Workspace Plugins (August 3, 2026)** — agents get direct read/write/act access to **Gmail, Google Drive, Calendar, Docs and Sheets** through Google's remote MCP servers. Drive: search, read, create, share and manage files. Gmail: search, read, draft, label and manage email. Calendar: list calendars and search events. Installed from the Cursor Marketplace or the Customize page in roughly five clicks. Source: https://cursor.com/changelog/google-workspace-plugins

platforms.name: Perplexity
details: **Gateway API (July 2026)** — a unified API gateway with **OpenAI Chat Completions and Anthropic Messages compatibility** and automatic health-based routing across model deployments, priced purely per token with no per-request fee. Source: https://docs.perplexity.ai/changelog

**Hosted remote MCP server at `https://api.perplexity.ai/mcp` (July 2026)** — cloud-hosted, no local installation, connected over Streamable HTTP with a Bearer API key. Exposes three tools: direct web search via the Search API, conversational AI backed by the Agent API `fast` preset, and deep research backed by the `high` preset. This resolves the "reference-only, no dated launch" watch item carried since 2026-07-07. Source: https://docs.perplexity.ai/docs/getting-started/integrations/mcp-server
*(Context, below bar: Agent API added Claude Opus 5, the full GPT-5.6 family, Gemini 3.6 Flash, Grok 4.5 and Kimi K3; Sonar Chat Completions consolidated into the Agent API.)*

platforms.name: Windsurf / Devin Desktop
details: **Browser Preview (ACP) and MCP OAuth authentication — v3.6.21 (July 29, 2026)** — remote agents can now reach **local development servers** through the built-in preview pane, and MCP servers requiring OAuth get a dedicated "Authenticate" button. The same release adds Plan Mode in Devin Local (explicit approval before implementation) and editable approvals that let a user modify a command before approving it or accept an AI-suggested rewrite. Source: https://docs.devin.ai/desktop/changelog

findings.title: AWS Agent Registry — GA on the `agent-registry` namespace
findings.description: AWS moved Agent Registry out of preview onto its own namespace on August 6, 2026, as a private governed catalog of agents, tools, skills, MCP servers and custom resources, reachable through the console, control-plane and data-plane APIs, and the registry's own MCP endpoint. This introduces a full set of new inventory entities — registry objects, registry records typed by the required `recordType`, record tags, per-registry authorization configs, and approval configs that gate whether a record becomes discoverable — plus new discovery APIs (`ListDiscoverableRegistryRecords`, `BatchGetDiscoverableRegistryRecord`) that AISPM can consume directly. Because record definitions are validated against the MCP and A2A schemas, the registry is also the authoritative map of which agents can talk to which tools. AISPM must discover these records, reconcile them against actually-deployed runtimes (registry-vs-reality drift and unregistered shadow agents are the toxic combination), and flag registries whose approval config allows records to become discoverable without review. Anyone still calling the old `bedrock-agentcore` endpoints must migrate IAM policies, SDK clients and registry data

findings.title: AgentCore Runtime "Instances" compute type with capacity providers
findings.description: A new AgentCore Runtime compute type that runs agents on AWS-managed EC2 inside the customer's own account, defined by a new **capacity provider** resource (operating system, allowed instance types, networking, storage). It introduces persistent agent sessions of up to **14 days**, GPU-accelerated instance types, and — most significantly — **multiple agents collaborating on a single shared instance**. That combination creates genuinely new posture questions Zenity does not model today: long-lived agent state that outlives any single task, cross-agent contamination on shared compute, and agent workloads sitting on customer-account EC2 with customer networking and IAM rather than on AWS-managed isolation. AISPM must inventory capacity providers, instance-backed runtimes and their session lifetimes, and map which agents co-tenant on which instance. New data-plane operation: `DeleteCapacityProviderSession`

findings.title: Anthropic inference hooks for Claude Enterprise (beta)
findings.description: Anthropic now lets an enterprise point Claude at its own AI security server, and every governed prompt across **claude.ai, Cowork and Claude Code** is held for that server's allow/deny verdict before inference proceeds. Requests are signed, failure handling is configurable, and every denial lands in the compliance Activity Feed. This is a new real-time enforcement chokepoint sitting in front of the model on a platform Zenity covers, and it is directly actionable in two ways: as a detection and enforcement integration point Zenity can occupy, and as a control whose configuration must itself be inventoried — which surfaces are actually governed, what the failure-handling mode does when the hook server is unreachable (fail-open versus fail-closed decides whether an outage is a bypass), and whether the Activity Feed denial stream is being ingested

findings.title: Microsoft Copilot Studio — Windows 365 for Agents MCP server (GA)
findings.description: A generally-available MCP server that gives a Copilot Studio agent full operational control of a Windows 365 Cloud PC: mouse and keyboard input, pixel-precise drag-and-drop, screen capture, OCR with bounding boxes, arbitrary command execution, browser automation through Microsoft Edge, and semantic UI inspection via Windows UI Automation. This is a new entity class for inventory — Windows 365 for Agents MCP server connections, the Cloud PC resources they allocate, and their `sessionId`-scoped sessions — and a materially larger blast radius than tool-calling: an agent driving a real Windows desktop inherits whatever that Cloud PC's signed-in identity can reach, including apps with no API. AISPM must discover which agents have this MCP server attached, which Cloud PCs they can allocate, and what the Cloud PC identity is entitled to. Note the file-input restriction to Documents, Downloads, Desktop and `%TEMP%` is the only documented filesystem boundary

findings.title: OpenAI GPT-5.6 model family — Sol, Terra, Luna (GA)
findings.description: OpenAI shipped a three-tier frontier/agentic model family on July 9, 2026 with model IDs `gpt-5.6-sol`, `gpt-5.6-terra` and `gpt-5.6-luna` (bare `gpt-5.6` routes to Sol), all with a 1.05M-token context window, 128K max output, and a reasoning effort ladder up to `max`. Access is self-serve on the Responses API with no waitlist or gating, so these IDs will appear in customer environments without any procurement signal. Sol is explicitly positioned for long-horizon agentic work. AISPM must add the three model IDs as inventory entities and treat the ungated, self-serve availability as the reason model-usage discovery cannot rely on approval workflows. This closes the forward-watch opened on the 2026-07-08 scan

findings.title: OpenAI Codex Agent Plugins and multi-catalog marketplace
findings.description: Codex CLI 0.146.0/0.147.0 introduce Agent Plugins — installable workflow bundles that each package **skills, optional app integrations and MCP server configuration** in one unit — installed from the official Plugin Directory (shared with ChatGPT), from a repo-level marketplace at `$REPO_ROOT/.agents/plugins/marketplace.json`, or from a personal marketplace at `~/.agents/plugins/marketplace.json`. This is a new local-extension entity type on a developer endpoint, and the repo-level marketplace is the sharp edge: cloning a repository can present plugins that carry MCP server configuration, meaning a plugin install is effectively a tool-and-connection grant sourced from version control. ENDPOINT must enumerate installed plugins per developer machine, resolve which marketplace each came from, and extract the MCP servers and app integrations each one wires up

findings.title: "Sign in with ChatGPT" identity provider (beta)
findings.description: OpenAI launched its first cross-platform identity system on August 2, 2026, with Airtable, GitLab, HubSpot, Notion, Supabase and Vercel as named partners plus OpenAI Academy and Codex Sites. It is available globally to authenticated ChatGPT users **including members of Enterprise organisations**, subject to org admin settings, and relying parties receive name, email address and profile picture. This makes ChatGPT an identity broker into third-party SaaS, which is a new class of entity for AISPM: ChatGPT-brokered account links, the relying parties consuming them, and the org admin setting that governs whether Enterprise members may use it at all. The risk to model is corporate identity sprawl created outside the IdP — accounts on GitLab or Notion provisioned via ChatGPT rather than the sanctioned SSO path, and therefore invisible to normal identity governance

findings.title: Claude Opus 5 across four hosting platforms
findings.description: Anthropic launched `claude-opus-5` on July 24, 2026 with a 1M-token context window as both default and maximum, 128k max output, thinking on by default, and an effort ladder through `xhigh` and `max`, explicitly positioned for long-running agents. It is simultaneously available on the Claude API, **Claude in Amazon Bedrock, Claude on Google Cloud (Vertex), and Claude in Microsoft Foundry** — four platforms Zenity already monitors separately. AISPM must add the model ID as an inventory entity on all four, and the 1M default context is worth modelling on its own: a default-maximum context materially raises how much organisational data a single agent turn can hold

findings.title: Claude Enterprise user management via the Admin API (beta)
findings.description: Anthropic opened programmatic management of a Claude Enterprise organisation — list members and look them up by email, change roles, remove members, send and withdraw invites, manage groups and their membership, and read custom roles (groups and custom roles behind the `ce-user-management-2026-07-13` header). This gives AISPM its first API-level read of Claude Enterprise identity: members, roles, groups, group membership and custom roles all become discoverable inventory entities rather than console-only state, enabling least-privilege analysis and orphaned-member detection on a primary platform. It cuts both ways — an Admin API key with `read:org_audit` can call every user-management `GET`, so these keys are now high-value credentials whose scope and holders need tracking

findings.title: Cursor Google Workspace plugins — agent access to Gmail, Drive and Calendar
findings.description: Cursor agents can now read, write and act across Gmail, Google Drive, Calendar, Docs and Sheets through Google's remote MCP servers, installed from the Cursor Marketplace in about five clicks. Drive access covers search, read, create, share and manage; Gmail covers search, read, draft, label and manage. This is the watching-tier finding that most clearly crosses into Zenity's core concern: a coding agent on a developer laptop now holds a direct path to corporate mail and file storage, with **share** permissions on Drive, and the install path requires no admin involvement. AISPM should treat Cursor-installed Workspace plugins as a discoverable connector entity and model the toxic combination of an IDE agent holding both source-code context and mail/file-exfiltration capability

findings.title: Google Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform — AlphaEvolve optimization service (GA)
findings.description: A code optimization and discovery agent, now GA, that iteratively generates mutated candidate programs server-side from a customer's baseline algorithm while **the customer's evaluation function runs client-side on their own infrastructure** and submits scores back. This is a new agent service to inventory on a secondary-tier platform, and its split-execution architecture is unusual enough to model explicitly: LLM-generated code is executed inside the customer's environment on every iteration, so the AlphaEvolve evaluator harness is an unmonitored code-execution path between a Google service and customer infrastructure. AISPM should discover AlphaEvolve jobs, their seed algorithms and their evaluator deployment locations

findings.title: AgentCore Gateway configurable rate limits
findings.description: AgentCore Gateway moved from service-managed rate limiting to customer-configurable limits scoped along JWT claims, IAM principals, target names, tool names and qualified model IDs, with request, token and connection metrics, wildcard catch-alls, most-specific-match-wins evaluation and `rate=0` as an explicit block. Six new operations create the limits as first-class configuration objects (`CreateRateLimit`, `GetRateLimit`, `UpdateRateLimit`, `DeleteRateLimit`, `ListRateLimits`, `BatchPutRateLimitEntries`). AISPM should inventory rate-limit objects as a per-gateway control and evaluate their coverage — a gateway with no caller-scoped entry has no multi-tenant isolation. Two properties deserve rules of their own: the system **fails open** on transient enforcement errors, and `rate=0` is the documented emergency caller-isolation mechanism, which makes its presence or absence a meaningful posture signal

findings.title: AgentCore Identity — Private Key JWT client authentication
findings.description: Agents can now authenticate to a downstream identity provider's token endpoint with a KMS-signed JWT client assertion instead of a shared OAuth client secret, across machine-to-machine, on-behalf-of and user-delegated flows (RS256, PS256, ES256). This introduces a new credential entity type for inventory — the registered public key, the KMS key backing it, and the OAuth client configured for Private Key JWT — replacing a secret Zenity would previously have tracked as a stored credential. It is also a posture improvement worth detecting: agents still using shared client secrets where Private Key JWT is available are now the weaker configuration, and because every signing operation is recorded in CloudTrail, KMS signing activity becomes a usable per-agent authentication signal

findings.title: AgentCore Evaluations — OpenAI Agents, LlamaIndex, Google ADK and Claude Agent SDK support
findings.description: AgentCore Evaluations now ingests telemetry from agents built on OpenAI Agents, LlamaIndex, Google ADK and the Claude Agent SDK alongside Strands and LangGraph, plus a generic path for any agent emitting OpenTelemetry GenAI or OpenInference semantic conventions. The security-relevant consequence is that AgentCore is now an observability plane for **third-party-framework agents that do not run on AgentCore Runtime** — meaning agent activity from four more frameworks becomes visible in an AWS-side telemetry surface. AIDR should treat these framework-tagged span streams as a new detection source and use the documented scope names and identifying attributes to attribute activity back to a specific agent and framework

findings.title: AgentCore Runtime unified span destination
findings.description: Agent spans now land in each agent's own CloudWatch log group (`/aws/bedrock-agentcore/runtimes/<agent_id>-<endpoint_name>`, `spans` stream) rather than the shared `aws/spans` group, and this is the **default for every agent created on or after July 20, 2026**. This is a breaking change for any collection that reads the shared group: agents created after that date will silently produce no spans there, creating a monitoring blind spot exactly on the newest agents. AIDR must switch to per-agent log groups, enumerate them by agent ID and endpoint name, and detect agents whose `UNIFIED_TRACES_DESTINATION_ENABLED` setting leaves them outside the expected collection path. The upside is that access control and encryption can now be scoped per agent

findings.title: AgentCore Harness streams MCP tool result metadata
findings.description: `InvokeHarness` previously dropped metadata attached to MCP tool results before it reached the client; it now streams on a dedicated `toolResultMetadata` delta channel, automatically split into ordered fragments for large payloads. This is a new data channel between MCP tools and agent clients that carries arbitrary tool-controlled JSON and was, until now, simply discarded. AIDR should capture and reassemble this channel — both because it is new agent-activity telemetry and because tool-controlled content flowing into an agent's context is a plausible injection carrier that no existing detection inspects

findings.title: AgentCore Gateway Web Search connector v1.2.0 — domain include lists and request-level filters
findings.description: The Web Search Tool connector adds a target-level domain **include** list alongside the existing exclude list (both raised from 20 to 100 domains) and per-request `filters` on each `tools/call`, covering `domainFilter.include`/`exclude` and a `publishedDateFilter`. These are new egress-scoping configuration entities on a tool Zenity already tracks: an include list is an allow-list boundary on where an agent may retrieve web content from, and its presence or absence is a posture signal. AISPM should inventory per-target include/exclude lists and flag Web Search targets with neither, since request-level filters are agent-supplied and cannot be relied on as a control

findings.title: Anthropic mid-conversation tool changes (beta)
findings.description: Tools can now be added or removed between turns of a conversation while preserving the prompt cache, on Fable 5, Mythos 5, Opus 4.8 and Opus 5, via the `mid-conversation-tool-changes-2026-07-01` header. An agent's tool set is no longer a fixed property established at conversation start — it becomes mutable state, so a point-in-time inventory of "which tools does this agent have" is no longer sufficient. AIRT should test whether a tool introduced mid-conversation inherits trust established earlier in the session, and whether cache preservation across a tool-set change lets earlier context influence a tool added afterwards. AISPM correspondingly needs per-turn rather than per-agent tool attribution

findings.title: Claude Managed Agents environment and memory-store lifecycle webhooks
findings.description: Managed Agents webhooks now cover four `environment.*` and three `memory_store.*` event types, on top of the agent, deployment and deployment-run events added June 30. Sessions can additionally be seeded with `initial_events` (up to 50 events, starting the agent loop in the same call) and session thread streams now support event deltas. These are new activity types AIDR can consume push-style rather than by polling — environment creation and teardown, and memory-store lifecycle changes, are exactly the events that reveal an agent gaining new execution context or a new persistent data store. Session seeding also matters for provenance: with `initial_events` the first turn of an agent loop can originate from an API caller rather than an interactive user, so event attribution must distinguish the two

findings.title: Claude Dreams — derived memory stores (backlog recovery)
findings.description: `POST /v1/dreams` runs an asynchronous job over one memory store plus up to 100 past session transcripts and produces a **new derived memory store** with duplicates merged, contradictions resolved and fresh insights surfaced. Dreams are first-class resources (`drm_01…` IDs, `pending`/`running`/`completed`/`failed`/`canceled` states, list/cancel/archive endpoints) gated behind the `dreaming-2026-04-21` beta header. The inventory consequence is data lineage: a dream reads session transcripts and writes their distilled content into a *different* store, so classification and access controls applied to the input store do not automatically hold on the output, and organisational content can propagate into a store nobody explicitly created. AISPM should discover dream jobs, map input stores and sessions to output stores, and flag derived stores whose access scope is broader than their inputs. Flagged as a coverage gap — Dreams has been live since roughly April 2026 and has never been reported by this monitor

findings.title: Claude Cowork — autonomous local-file desktop agent (backlog recovery)
findings.description: Cowork is an autonomous desktop agent built on the same agentic architecture as Claude Code that reads and writes **local files** in user-designated folders and plans and executes multi-step task sequences without a prompt at every turn, now on macOS, web and mobile with cloud task execution in beta. It is aimed squarely at non-technical staff — operations, project management, department heads — which means an agent with local filesystem write access is being deployed to populations with no developer-endpoint controls and outside whatever coverage exists for Claude Code. ENDPOINT must detect Cowork installations, enumerate the folders it has been pointed at, and distinguish local from cloud execution. Note that Cowork is one of the three surfaces governed by the new inference hooks, so hook coverage and Cowork inventory should be reconciled. Flagged as a coverage gap — Cowork launched January 2026 and has never been reported by this monitor

findings.title: OpenAI Codex — MCP 2026-07-28, executor-provided skills discovery and remote WebSocket code mode
findings.description: Codex CLI added support for MCP protocol revision 2026-07-28 with paginated tool discovery, executor-provided skills discovery, remote WebSocket code-mode connections, and migration paths that import Cursor skills and synchronise Claude conversations. Each is a distinct endpoint surface: paginated discovery means a server's full tool list is no longer visible in a single response and must be walked to enumerate completely; executor-provided skills are capabilities injected by the execution environment rather than declared in local configuration; and remote WebSocket code mode is a persistent outbound channel from the developer machine. The cross-tool migrations mean skills and conversation history now move between vendor agents, so provenance does not stop at the tool boundary

findings.title: OpenAI Codex automatic approval reviews (`--approve-for-me`)
findings.description: Codex CLI 0.147.0 adds a flag that delegates approval decisions to the model itself, shipped two days after 0.146.1 patched in "safer automatic-review defaults for cyber-capable models" — the sequencing indicates OpenAI treats automated approval as security-sensitive. Removing the human from the approval loop turns every approval prompt into a model decision that an attacker can attempt to influence, making this a direct prompt-injection escalation path: content injected into a repository, a tool result or a web page reaches the same model that decides whether the next command runs. AIRT should build cases that attempt to steer auto-approval into executing commands a human would have rejected, and specifically probe whether the cyber-capable-model defaults hold under injected content

findings.title: OpenAI content provenance checks API
findings.description: The Python (v2.52.0) and Node (v7.3.0) SDKs added programmatic content-provenance verification, checking C2PA Content Credentials and Google SynthID watermarks on images and, since July 2026, audio generated through ChatGPT, Codex and the OpenAI API. This is a new API surface to inventory, and a usable detection primitive: provenance checks let an organisation determine whether a given asset originated from OpenAI tooling, which is directly relevant to establishing whether AI-generated content entered a workflow. AISPM should track which applications call it and treat provenance-verification results as an attribute on discovered content artefacts

findings.title: OpenAI admin spend-limit and organisational service-account key management APIs
findings.description: Recent SDK releases expose admin APIs for organisational spend limits and, more importantly for security, **service-account key management endpoints**. Service-account keys are non-human credentials that authenticate automated workloads against OpenAI, and an API to create and manage them means they can now be provisioned programmatically and at scale. AISPM should enumerate service accounts and their keys as inventory entities, attribute API usage to them, and detect keys that are unused, over-permissioned or created outside a sanctioned process — a service-account key is the most likely credential to outlive the person who created it

findings.title: Microsoft Copilot Studio — Foundry IQ knowledge connection and agent-to-agent delegation in the new agent experience
findings.description: Two preview capabilities extend the Copilot Studio agent graph across a boundary. Agents can now be grounded in an **Azure AI Foundry** knowledge base via Foundry IQ, and a front-door agent in the new agent experience can delegate to specialist agents. Together they mean a Copilot Studio agent's effective data reach and effective capability set are no longer determined by its own configuration: knowledge flows in from a different Microsoft product with its own permission model, and capability flows in from other agents. AISPM must resolve Foundry IQ knowledge-base bindings as cross-product data-access edges and build the full delegation graph, since a front-door agent inherits the reach of every specialist beneath it — the classic transitive over-privilege case

findings.title: Microsoft 365 Copilot — Insights Agent (preview)
findings.description: A new first-party agent has appeared under "Create and manage agents" in the Microsoft 365 Copilot extensibility documentation, absent from the previous capture. First-party agents are enabled tenant-side rather than built by a maker, so they arrive in customer tenants without appearing in any maker-created agent inventory. AISPM should add Insights Agent to the first-party agent inventory for M365 Copilot, determine what organisational data it is grounded in, and confirm it is covered by the same discovery path used for declarative and custom-engine agents

findings.title: Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform — Memory Bank Memory Profiles (GA)
findings.description: Memory profiles are structured data objects with fixed, user-defined schemas that LLMs populate and update, generated through the same `GenerateMemories` and `IngestEvents` paths as natural-language memories and held for low-latency in-session access. This is a distinct new memory entity type from free-text memories: a profile has a declared schema, which means the organisation has explicitly specified what categories of information about a user or entity get extracted and persisted. AISPM should inventory profile schemas alongside memory stores, since the schema itself is the disclosure — a schema field naming a sensitive attribute is a standing instruction to extract that attribute from every session. Memory Bank and Sessions multi-regional and global endpoints also went GA, which affects where this data resides

findings.title: Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform — Feedback service (preview) and `user.id` in agent logs
findings.description: The Feedback service collects, analyses and manages end-user qualitative feedback (thumbs up/down sentiment, feedback labels) from agent–user interactions, and separately, prompt-input and response-output agent logs now carry a `user.id` field when that logging is enabled. The logging change is the operationally significant one: agent prompt and response logs become **user-attributable**, turning an anonymous content stream into a per-identity activity trail that AIDR can use to attribute prompts and data access to specific people. The feedback corpus is a second new activity surface, and it stores end-user free text — worth treating as a data store in its own right rather than as metrics

findings.title: Perplexity Gateway API and hosted remote MCP server
findings.description: Perplexity shipped a unified API gateway that is **wire-compatible with both OpenAI Chat Completions and Anthropic Messages**, with automatic health-based routing across model deployments, and made its MCP server available cloud-hosted at `https://api.perplexity.ai/mcp` over Streamable HTTP with a Bearer key. The gateway is the finding that matters beyond the watching tier: OpenAI- and Anthropic-shaped traffic can now be pointed at Perplexity by changing a base URL, so traffic that looks like sanctioned OpenAI or Anthropic API usage may not be reaching those vendors at all. AISPM and AIDR should treat base-URL/endpoint attribution as part of model-usage discovery rather than inferring the provider from request shape. The hosted MCP server removes the local-install signal that previously made Perplexity MCP usage detectable on endpoints, and resolves the reference-only watch item carried since 2026-07-07

findings.title: Windsurf / Devin Desktop — remote-agent access to local dev servers and MCP OAuth authentication
findings.description: v3.6.21 lets **remote agents reach local development servers** through the built-in Browser Preview (ACP) pane, and adds a dedicated "Authenticate" button for MCP servers requiring OAuth. The browser preview creates a path from a cloud-hosted agent into services bound to the developer's local machine — typically unauthenticated dev servers holding real data and credentials, sitting behind no network control because they were never expected to be reachable from outside. MCP OAuth authentication means MCP server connections now carry delegated user authorisation, so an MCP connection on this endpoint can hold real access tokens to third-party services. ENDPOINT should enumerate MCP servers configured in Devin Desktop along with their OAuth grants, and treat remote-agent-to-localhost as a distinct data-flow to monitor
